subject: Discovery recap & proposed bakeoff scope — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@nimbusai.com>, Nina Park <nina.park@nimbusai.com>
Cc: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:10:00 -0800
Subject: Discovery recap & proposed bakeoff scope — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints

Hi Ethan / Nina — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed execution plan for the competitive evaluation you asked for. I captured pain points, success criteria, and a minimal bakeoff matrix so we can align on what to measure.

Key pain points you shared
- Inconsistent latency at scale during peak inference windows (notably p95 spikes)
- High per-token costs on current managed cloud endpoints during batch-heavy workloads
- Difficulty reproducing model quality parity when moving from prototype (vLLM on local) to a managed endpoint (TGI / cloud)
- Need for predictable autoscaling & clear failure modes (graceful fallback when capacity constrained)

Success criteria (what Nimbus told us would make this a win)
- Latency: p95 text-generation latency < 200ms for 1–2k token sequences at pilot tps (50–150 RPS burst)
- Cost: baseline per-1k-token inference cost lower than current cloud endpoint by >= 20% for comparable config
- Quality: semantic similarity on your benchmark set >= 0.88 vs your internal golden outputs (we can accept >0.85 initially if you want progressive improvement checks)
- Operational: deterministic autoscaling behavior and predictable KV cache warmup under simulated traffic

Proposed bakeoff matrix (high-level) — we propose to run the following tests in parallel across implementations you mentioned (your vLLM baseline, TGI-managed endpoint, cloud vendor endpoint, and Redwood hosted/dedicated):
1) Latency histogram & p50/p95/p99 under steady-state and burst (50/150/300 RPS)
2) Throughput and concurrency at target latency SLOs (tokens/sec, concurrent requests)
3) Token cost estimate (synthetic & real prompt mix) at different batch sizes / quantization profiles
4) Output quality: semantic similarity + hallucination rate on your provided eval prompts + a human spot-check sample
5) Memory/CPU/GPU utilization and KV-cache efficiency (memory growth over long conversations)
6) Failure modes: cold-start/resume behavior, queueing/backpressure, and fallback correctness

What we need from your side (asks)
- Share a representative prompt set and evaluation labels (attach as sample_prompts_nimbus.json if possible)
- Provide a target traffic pattern (RPS profile) and the list of model weights/architecture you want tested (e.g., Llama 2 13B q4, etc.)
- Confirm whether Redwood should run tests from our dedicated infra or if you want us to run agents in your VPC for parity with your vLLM environment

Proposed timeline
- Nov 30–Dec 2: align on dataset + acceptance criteria
- Dec 3–7: run parallel benchmarks and collect metrics
- Dec 8: share results deck + raw metrics + runbook for reproducibility

Next steps / owners
- Aditya (me): finalize scope & coordinate test access (owner)
- Vivek: solution engineering — building the benchmark harness and running Redwood lanes
- Monica: CS lead for definition of quality metrics and human spot checks
- Ethan / Nina: provide prompt set, current baseline metrics, and confirm preferred test environment

Attachments: redwood_bakeoff_matrix_v1.xlsx (test cases + measurement plan), sample_prompts_nimbus.json, nimbus_mvp_requirements.pdf (your doc from the call)

Open question: do you want us to include a Terraform-based reproducible harness to run in your VPC, or is it fine to run from Redwood-managed infra for the initial pass?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 15m sync to finalize the scope.

Best,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_bakeoff_matrix_v1.xlsx (XLSX, 18KB)]
[Attachment: sample_prompts_nimbus.json (JSON, 12KB)]
From: Ethan Zhao <ethan.zhao@nimbusai.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nina Park <nina.park@nimbusai.com>, procurement@nimbusai.com
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 18:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Discovery recap & proposed bakeoff scope — Redwood vs vLLM/TGI/cloud endpoints

Aditya — thanks for the thorough note and the matrix. This aligns with our expectations. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) Prompt set: attached a trimmed set (sample_prompts_nimbus_subset.json) — it includes 120 prompts across support, summarization, and retrieval-augmented Q&A. We will provide the full set (2.5k prompts) early next week.
2) Baseline models: we are running vLLM locally on our infra (Llama 2 13B q4 and an in-house fine-tuned 7B). Our cloud baseline is managed TGI on VendorX and a standard managed endpoint from CloudY.
3) Environment: for parity we'd prefer Redwood run the initial pass in our VPC (we can provide a temporary STS role) so we can validate networking/throughput impacts. If that turns out to be heavy, fallback to Redwood-managed infra is fine for an iterative run.

Acceptance tweaks: we can bump the quality target to >= 0.87 for the first run and move to >= 0.88 on the second iteration. Also confirm whether your cost calc includes GPU amortization or purely per-request compute cost.

I'll loop in procurement next week for an NDA/PO if needed. We aim to make a decision by mid-December.

—Ethan
[Attachment: sample_prompts_nimbus_subset.json (JSON, 6KB)]
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 08:53:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: Nimbus bakeoff — follow-up and action items (owner assignments)

Team — forwarding the client reply and their preliminary prompt subset. High-level notes and asks: 

- They want the initial run in their VPC (they will provide temporary STS role). We'll need a minimal Terraform/CloudFormation harness to deploy the benchmark agent and chain to their vLLM/TGI endpoints. Vivek: can you draft the infra plan (IAM role, instance types, network egress) and confirm whether we can run our harness without persistent infra in their account?
- Quality target: start with >=0.87, aim for >=0.88 on iteration two. Monica: define scoring rubric (semantic similarity metric, threshold for hallucination) and estimate human spot-check sample size.
- Cost calc: confirm whether to include GPU amortization; I think we present both amortized and per-request compute to be transparent. Aisha: you own the pricing narrative (compare to their VendorX cloud baseline and show Redwood Dedicated vs Hosted).

Deliverables this week: infra plan (Vivek), quality rubric + human sample plan (Monica), pricing comparison draft (Aisha). I will continue coordinating with Ethan on access and timeline.

Laura — looping you since this is a potential mid-6-figure dedicated deal if we win. Happy to sync after we have the run results.

Thanks,
Aditya
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Internal: Nimbus bakeoff — follow-up and action items (owner assignments)

Quick confirmation — I'll own the infra harness. Plan outline: 
- Day 0: get STS role / temp creds from Nimbus (no long-lived keys).
- Day 1: deploy lightweight benchmark agent ( ECS task / k8s job ) that can hit their vLLM/TGI endpoints and our Redwood lanes for parity. We'll provision spot-capable GPU instances (A10G-equivalent) and limit runtime to the test window.
- Metrics collected: request/response latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU memory usage, token throughput, and per-request cost estimates (we'll produce both amortized and incremental compute cost).
- Reproducibility: publish a small terraform module (no secrets), plus a runbook and raw csvs to the Drive link in the thread.

I'll start drafting the terraform module today and share a short PR by EOD tomorrow. HubSpot link for the deal is in the related links I added to the thread.

-Vivek
